citations.description: test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness: rotates registry + unscoped head drift → stale-head, not stale-code
test_compute_validity_still_catches_a_real_code_drift: dep file drift → stale-code, but no registry rotation

findings.criterion: stale-code, stale-head, stale-material and stale-reopened still return valid: False — proven by a test that rotates the registry AND drifts a dependency file on one attestation and asserts the verdict is stale-code.
findings.detail: No single test combines registry rotation AND dependency-file drift to assert stale-code. The closest test, test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness (test_compute_validity.py:123), rotates the registry but uses an unscoped attestation (no dep lines), so the verdict is stale-head, not stale-code. The test test_compute_validity_still_catches_a_real_code_drift (test_opcert_local_verify_binding.py:363) proves stale-code still blocks but does not simultaneously rotate the registry. The AC explicitly requires a single test that does both.

citations.description: Ticket comment: 'Gates: make lint + make typecheck clean; 6738 passed / 31 skipped across tests/unit + tests/interfaces.' — not admissible for a codebase-verifiable criterion.

findings.criterion: make lint, make typecheck and the full pytest suite pass in the worktree.
findings.detail: This criterion is not tagged [operator-attested], so it is codebase-verifiable. It is a runtime check (executing make lint, make typecheck, pytest) that cannot be verified from code inspection alone. The ticket comment attests 'Gates: make lint + make typecheck clean; 6738 passed / 31 skipped' but a ticket comment is not admissible evidence for a codebase-verifiable criterion.
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion [operator-attested] and record the CI run URL/id, the exact pass/fail counts, and the timestamp as a ticket comment. Alternatively, if the criterion is intended to be codebase-verifiable, a CI artifact or test result file in the repo would be needed.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
